chapter_title: The Chapter of the Commandments of Righteousness
chapter_note: This chapter is overwhelmingly an institutional/disciplinary summary (elect vs. catechumens, fasting/prayer/alms, giving persons/buildings to the church). Although it contains Manichaean cosmological terms (e.g., Cross of Light; sun and moon as light-givers), they function here as rationale within commandments rather than as impersonal cosmos→cosmos correspondential exposition. No recoverable pre-compilation systematic teaching substrate is present; the opening is explicitly framed, and the latter paragraphs show strong editorial/institutional extension.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Begins with a hagiographic dialogue attribution (“[Once more] the enlightener speaks…”), then immediately moves into prescriptive righteousness/seal-like discipline (continence; ‘rest of the hands’ before the Cross of Light; purity of mouth; no flesh/blood/wine). This is institutional rule-setting rather than impersonal cosmological mapping.

Ethical/institutional exhortation about multiplying and distributing wisdom/faith/grace to others (‘give wisdom… give faith… give freely of love’). No systematic cosmological architecture; reads as community edification material.
Explicitly organizes status categories (elect vs. catechumen) and perfection ‘in two stages’. This is church-structural language, not substrate cosmology.

Catechumenate rule triad (fasting, prayer, almsgiving) with liturgical/institutional anchoring (“lord’s day”, alms placed ‘in the holy one’). Even ‘pray to the sun and the moon’ appears as prescribed practice, not cosmic mechanics.

Institutional obligations to the church framed as meritorious acts (give a child/relative/slave to the church; rescue/buy and give; sharing in ‘good works’). Cosmos is not being expounded—social practice is.
Practical institutional benefaction (“build a dwelling… portion of alms in the holy church”). This is operational church material.

Flagged editorial extension: recap and amplification of catechumen alms within ‘holy church’ benefits (‘catechumens… share of every grace and good in the holy church’). The entire paragraph is an institutional payoff statement extending the preceding list, not an older teaching fragment.
